## Accounting's Existential Talent Problem

The American Institute of CPAs reported that CPA exam candidates declined 33% between 2016 and 2025. Simultaneously, 75% of AICPA members reached retirement eligibility by 2025. The profession faces a perfect storm.

### Why Students Are Choosing Other Paths

| Deterrent | Impact Score (1-10) |
|---|---|
| 150-credit-hour requirement for CPA | 9 |
| Starting salaries vs. tech | 8 |
| Perceived work-life balance issues | 8 |
| Busy season culture | 7 |
| Career ceiling perception | 6 |

### Salary Comparison: Accounting vs. Tech (Entry Level)

| Role | Year 1 Comp | Year 3 Comp | Year 5 Comp |
|---|---|---|---|
| Big Four Audit Associate | $65K | $82K | $105K |
| Corporate Staff Accountant | $58K | $72K | $88K |
| Software Engineer | $95K | $125K | $155K |
| Data Analyst | $72K | $90K | $115K |

### How Leading Firms Are Responding

- Reducing CPA dependency : Creating career tracks for non-CPA professionals in advisory and technology roles
- Signing bonuses : Big Four now offering $10-15K signing bonuses for experienced hires, up from zero five years ago
- Flexible work models : Year-round remote options with in-person collaboration during planning season
- Automation investment : Using AI for routine tasks, allowing staff to focus on advisory work
- Alternative talent pools : Hiring from finance, data science, and even liberal arts backgrounds with accounting boot camp programs
